claims.text: The baseline system is an elemental Cr coating on a zirconium-alloy cladding substrate.
Elemental Cr coatings can peel and crack during high-temperature steam oxidation.
Elevated-temperature Cr–Zr interdiffusion causes premature failure of the Cr coating.
A thin Al-rich interlayer should be deposited between the zirconium-alloy substrate and the elemental Cr coating.
At elevated temperature, the buried Al-rich interlayer will oxidize preferentially.
Preferential oxidation of the interlayer will produce a continuous, adherent Al2O3 scale at the Cr–Zr interface.
The interfacial Al2O3 scale will be stable and protective during accident-relevant high-temperature steam exposure.
The dense Al2O3 scale will act as a physical diffusion barrier to Cr and Zr.
Limiting Cr–Zr interdiffusion will mitigate premature coating failure.
Al-containing coating designs can improve corrosion protection of zirconium-alloy cladding under PWR-relevant conditions.
The Al-rich interlayer will not adversely affect the Cr coating's integrity or corrosion resistance under normal PWR conditions.
Relative to the unmodified Cr-coated baseline, the Al-interlayer coating will have a reduced Cr–Zr interdiffusion depth after transient high-temperature steam exposure.
Relative to the unmodified baseline, the Al-interlayer coating will exhibit less oxide degradation and better oxidation performance in high-temperature steam.
The modified coating will maintain corrosion resistance similar to the pure Cr coating during long-term subcritical-water exposure.
Normal-operation conditions are defined as PWR primary water below 350°C.
Accident conditions are defined as transient high-temperature steam exposure above 1200°C.
The optimal Al concentration and interlayer thickness, and the alumina scale's durability under thermal cycling, remain uncertain.
